cards.explanation: The three are Peter, James and John. Jesus took them up a high mountain by themselves (Mark 9:2). No crowd, no tour group, just those three and Jesus. I bet they had no idea what kind of hike they'd signed up for, friends.

The answer is True. Mark says His clothes became radiantly white, "…brighter than any launderer on earth could bleach them." (Mark 9:3) A launderer is someone who cleans clothes for a living. Those folks scrub all day, and they still couldn't touch this.

The two men are Elijah and Moses. They appeared before the three disciples, talking with Jesus (Mark 9:4). The text doesn't tell us what they said. Three disciples watching this, and I bet it was a lot to take in.

The answer is False, because the three shelters weren't for the disciples. Peter said, "Let us put up three shelters—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah." (Mark 9:5) So the shelters were for Jesus, Moses and Elijah. Not one of the three had Peter's name on it, friends.

The word is terrified. Mark says, "…they were all so terrified that Peter did not know what else to say." (Mark 9:6) They weren't just nervous, they were all terrified. Mark puts that right after Jesus was transfigured and Moses and Elijah appeared with Him.

The voice is talking about Jesus. The voice from the cloud says, "This is My beloved Son. Listen to Him!" (Mark 9:7) Moses and Elijah were right there, yet the voice points to Jesus. A voice from a cloud will get your attention fast, bakers.

The answer is False. Mark says, "Suddenly, when they looked around, they saw no one with them except Jesus." (Mark 9:8) Moses and Elijah were gone, and only Jesus was left with the three. They went up with Him, and they came down with Him.

Jesus told them to tell no one until the Son of Man had risen from the dead. Mark says He told them "…not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead." (Mark 9:9) Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). So Jesus put a limit on the silence, and the limit was His rising from the dead.

The scribes say Elijah must come first. The disciples ask, "Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?" (Mark 9:11) The scribes were Israel's teachers of the law. The three had just seen Elijah on the mountain with Jesus, so I think the question was sitting heavy on them. Jesus answers right away, and He doesn't dodge it.

What is written is that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected. Jesus asks, "Why then is it written that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected?" (Mark 9:12) He was talking about Himself, and He said it plainly. Sometimes the best answer to a question is a harder question, friends.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "But I tell you that Elijah has indeed come, and they have done to him whatever they wished, just as it is written about him." (Mark 9:13) He says it plainly after answering their question. Notice that He ties it to what is written.
